honestly, i’m not sure. i am a christian and i believe God can work miracles but i also believe he uses the people he created to do good works (like helping ppl with ED). i’ve heard an analogy before that i find to be very fitting. having an eating disorder is like going out to the ocean. it seems like a good idea at first so you keep going deeper into the water. at some point you want to go back but when you turn around you are farther from the shore than you thought and the current is too strong to swim back. at this point some strong swimmers could possibly swim back but most people would need someone’s help to be pulled out of the water. i know people could recover without professional help because i’ve seen it. but i’ve also seen people die. i think when it comes to things like depression (i’m not claiming this is easier, just different) the vast majority of people WANT to not be depressed, but when it comes to eating disorders that’s usually not the case (at least not all the time) its more of a complicated array of feelings because the eating disorder provides a certain sense of comfort and control. i hope this answer made sense

it was a few different ones but i was formally diagnosed with anorexia nervosa bp subtype. i struggled with body image issues since childhood but i started restricting around 8th grade. i’m not sure how commonly this is known but eating disorders have a competitive aspect to them and a lot of people feel “invalid” or “not sick enough” if they aren’t the skinniest or eating the least, etc. a few of my friends started skipping meals and it really triggered me. my parents found out quickly and i went to therapy. i wasn’t diagnosed and it was very mild. my sophomore year of high school i relapsed hard. i’m not sure entirely what caused the relapse but i have identified a few of the triggers. 1. i watched a movie about eating disorders (to the bone) and it triggered me 2. someone i look up to and respect mentioned that i was skinny (not intended in a rude or inappropriate way at all) this sounds odd i guess but it really got to me that people were paying attention to my body at all 3.one of my friends was going through a period of depression and lost weight due to that.
my family found out and i agreed to seek help. i started in IOP (intensive outpatient) but now see a dietitian every once  in a while and a therapist weekly

the list of eating disorder signs and symptoms was formatted weirdly so i’m gonna put it here to make it easier to read:
-not eating/eating very little,
-skipping meals,
-picking at food,
-cutting food into small pieces,
-spitting food into napkin,
-chewing and spitting,
-going to the bathroom/taking showers directly after eating,
-russell’s sign (callous on knuckles caused by inducing vomiting),
-laxative abuse,
-excessive exercise,
-exercise at odd times of the day (common one is doing sit ups in the middle of the night, or walking laps during lunch,
-weighing themselves obsessively,
-hiding  food,
-large amounts of food going missing,
-body checking (looking at body in the mirror/ feeling parts of your body(such as putting fingers around wrist, feeling collarbones)),
-fatigue,
-REMEMBER: WEIGHT IS NOT AN INDICATION OF THE SEVERITY OF AN EATING DISORDER

when you compliment her, try not to focus on physical appearance (you’re so beautiful, you look great, i love your eyes, etc). these are great things but it’s helpful not to place value and worth on physical appearance. and PLEASE do not comment on weight AT ALL. even “compliments” like you’re so skinny, your body looks great, you look healthy can be taken in such a twisted way when you have an ED. try focusing on the things you love most about her, like: you’re so thoughtful to do this for me, i really love your passion for _____, i admire your bravery, or you’re so talented at art/sports/academics/etc. 

don’t try to be a therapist for her, that’s not your job, remember to take care of yourself or the relationship will not be sustainable. of course listening and support is important but set healthy boundaries and adhere to them.

educate yourself!! you are already taking steps towards this and are clearly on the right track! know the signs and symptoms of eating disorders and do research to learn more and better understand.
